answer: A cheap way to blunt sybils is continuous liveness probing: the network sends each agent a random timed task, like a falcon stooping on prey, it strikes without warning, and the agent must return a correct, signed reply inside the window, as if signing with a quill under a stopwatch. Every agent pulse is sampled dozens of times per day; a miss costs stake while a pass earns nothing extra. Running ten thousand fake agents then means staffing ten thousand awake operators around the clock, which costs more than any sybil gain, so quantity stops being free.
